ShortDescription.Value: Real timetables for public transport — fixed departures, auto-sized fleets and terminus timing points. Works for buses, trams, trains, metros, ferries and planes.

Publish.LongDescription:
Turn any public-transport line into a scheduled service. Works for every passenger type: buses, trams, trains, metros, ferries and aircraft.
Per line you opt in and set:
- a first departure time and peak / off-peak / night intervals (the global peak windows are configurable), - OR give a line its OWN peak hours: any line can override the global rush with two custom windows and its own peak interval, so a line serving a factory shift, a school run or a stadium can run its own rush hour while the rest of the network keeps to the city-wide one, - the mod then DERIVES how many vehicles the line needs to hold that headway, and raises the game's vehicle-count ceiling so the derived fleet is never clamped, - a terminus stop (timing point) where early vehicles are held to the scheduled departure, and where surplus vehicles retire — after finishing their loop and dropping passengers, not mid-route.
Select any stop to open a printed-timetable departure board for every line that serves it, listed from the first departure of the day. Day-only and night-only lines only show and run the intervals that apply to them, and a night line is scheduled inside the night window.
No timetable set = the line runs exactly like vanilla. Everything is controlled from the line's own info panel plus a floating departures board.
SETTINGS (a plain timetable needs none of them):
- "Realistic travel time" (free, off by default): the game's own loop estimate is optimistic (it ignores the time vehicles lose braking, accelerating and loading passengers at every stop — real loops measure up to 3x it), so posted times drift ahead of reality. Turn this on and the mod measures each line's REAL loop as it runs and posts realistic stop times, so early vehicles wait at each stop until their true departure. Measurements are saved with your city, so they survive quitting instead of re-learning every session. Recommended, and it costs nothing. - "Provision fleet for real travel time" (increases number of vehicles, off by default): also sizes each line's vehicle count to its real loop. A line whose real loop is ~2x the estimate needs about twice the vehicles to hold the same headway. Grow-only and capped. - "Stop at every stop (even empty ones)" (free, off by default): by default a bus skips a stop where nobody boards or alights, so that stop isn't held to schedule; the terminus is now always honoured, and this extends that to every stop. Lines run a little slower. - "Maximum stop time" for buses and for rail (3 minutes each by default): how long a vehicle may keep waiting PAST its posted departure for passengers who are already boarding. It is a limit, not a target — a vehicle with nobody boarding still leaves exactly on its posted minute, and this setting never delays it by a second. Raise the rail value if you see people piling up on a busy platform: a train or metro exchanging a full platform takes far longer to load, and unlike a bus it can never skip a stop. Set it to 0 to leave on the dot and wait for nobody. - "Realistic Trips / slow-time compatibility" (ALPHA, off by default): keeps timing correct if you run a mod that lengthens the in-game day (Time2Work / Realistic Trips). Leave off otherwise.
CLEAN UNINSTALL: Options has a "Remove all mod data from this save" button. It reverts every line to the base game and deletes the mod's data from your city, so you can uninstall with nothing left behind. It clears your timetables, so it asks first — and after confirming, let the game run for a moment before you save.
Recommended: for accurate timetables at no cost, turn on "Realistic travel time" and leave the rest at their defaults; add "Provision fleet" only if you want the mod to also buy the vehicles that headway really needs, and raise "Maximum stop time" if you see passengers piling up on a busy platform.
KNOWN ISSUES:
- "Vehicles no longer un-bunch after removing the mod." The mod writes two values into a line's save data — an "unbunching factor" (an early pre-v0.2.3 build), and a "vehicle interval" it uses to size the fleet. If you remove or disable the mod WITHOUT first switching a line's timetable off, those values can stay frozen in the save (the base game never resets them), so vehicles leave a stop immediately without spacing out. FIXED as of v0.3.2.2: the mod now repairs both automatically on load, for every line, and safely — the vehicle interval is rebuilt from the line's own settings, so a count you set by hand with "Assigned Vehicles" is preserved. To repair an affected save: subscribe to v0.3.2.2 (or newer), load your city, then save. Normal unbunching returns, and you can keep or remove the mod afterwards.
CREDITS: per-line custom peak windows (each line can override the global peak hours and run its own peak interval) were contributed by incconutwo. Thank you. Community bug reports have driven several releases, including the terminus stop fix, the mid-route spawn fix and the missed-trip catch-up.
Source (open source, MIT): https://github.com/AmicusDeus/TransitTimetables
Localized into 11 languages (German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese-BR, Russian, Chinese Simplified & Traditional). Translations are machine-generated — corrections welcome.
Made with Claude Code's Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 models.
Publish.ChangeLog:
v0.4.1 [BETA] — Vehicles no longer leave passengers behind at the door
Still marked BETA: this changes how vehicles depart and how stop times are calculated. It has been reviewed line by line but not played through a long test. Please report anything odd on GitHub. If something misbehaves you can step back without uninstalling: "Maximum stop time" to 0 restores the old departure behaviour, "Realistic travel time" off restores the game's own estimates, "Manage vehicle count" off hands vehicle counts back, and the master switch pauses the whole mod.
- FIX: vehicles were throwing off passengers who were already boarding. Reported as "the bus fills up, then empties down to a certain amount, then leaves", with the queue growing at busy stations. Cause: the base game counts someone as a passenger the moment they START WALKING to the vehicle, so the mod's on-time departure was cancelling everyone still crossing the platform and putting them back in the queue. It happened on every departure of every timetabled vehicle. (Reported by a community member — thank you.)
- CHANGE: "Minimum stop time" is now "Maximum stop time", and it works the other way round. Instead of padding every stop, it now caps how long a vehicle may keep waiting PAST its posted departure for people who are already boarding. It is a limit, not a target: a vehicle with nobody boarding still leaves exactly on its posted minute and this setting never delays it. Both default to 3 minutes. Set it to 0 for the old "leave on the dot, wait for nobody" behaviour. Under the bonnet this now uses the game's own boarding logic rather than overriding it, so waiting, boarding order and the widening pick-up radius are all stock behaviour — the mod only decides when the game gives up.
- FIX: posted stop times could run backwards along a route (a later stop showing an earlier time) while some stops had measured times and others were still using the estimate. Times are now always non-decreasing around the loop.
v0.4.0 [BETA] — Missed trips, saved travel times and a clean uninstall
- NEW: missed trips are caught up. If a scheduled departure passes with no vehicle at the terminus, the next one to arrive now covers the gap instead of cancelling the trip and waiting for its own next slot, which used to leave vehicles parked at the terminus while the line ran empty. Guarded so it cannot bunch with the following departure. - NEW: measured travel times are saved with your city, so they survive quitting instead of being re-learned from scratch every session. Posted stop times are therefore right from the moment you load rather than after a day or two of measuring. - NEW: "Remove all mod data from this save" button (Options > General) for a clean uninstall with nothing left behind. - FIX: a vehicle could retire at a stop SHARED with another line while nothing of its own line was there to take the next departure. - FIX: vehicles could disappear mid-route instead of finishing their loop, because the mod stopped protecting them whenever a line was already at its target count. - FIX: lines could shed vehicles below their target; the retirement list is now rebuilt as the target changes. - FIX: assorted fleet issues — the mod and the game could disagree about a line's target count after loading, the per-line vehicle cap now applies on every path, and a diagnostic message no longer repeats every few frames.
v0.3.5 — Optional "Manage vehicle count" toggle, so a dedicated fleet mod can own vehicle counts instead.
v0.3.4 — Localized into 11 languages. Machine-translated, community corrections welcome.
